B1-GEN-01-1.title: FAISS wiki: Guidelines to choose an index
B1-GEN-01-1.supports: nlist range, HNSW memory formula, HNSW being fast and accurate, PQ needing a re-ranking stage, and HNSW lacking vector removal.

B1-GEN-01-1.title: FAISS wiki: Faiss indexes
B1-GEN-01-1.supports: HNSW deletion is not natively supported in FAISS, consistent with deletes being awkward.

B1-GEN-01-1.title: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search using Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs
B1-GEN-01-1.supports: HNSW is built incrementally as a multi-layer proximity graph and was reported to strongly outperform earlier open-source vector-only methods.

B1-GEN-01-1.title: ANN-Benchmarks
B1-GEN-01-1.supports: On the benchmarked datasets, very different ANN approaches gave comparable quality-performance trade-offs, which motivates measuring recall-latency curves on your own data.

B1-GEN-01-3.title: FAISS wiki: MetricType and distances
B1-GEN-01-3.supports: Squared-L2 return, cosine requires normalisation, L2/IP equivalence on unit vectors.

B1-GEN-01-3.title: Model card: sentence-transformers/multi-qa-mpnet-base-dot-v1
B1-GEN-01-3.supports: Some encoders are intended for dot product and emit unnormalised vectors.

B1-GEN-01-4.title: Towards Backward-Compatible Representation Learning (Shen et al., 2020)
B1-GEN-01-4.supports: Updating an embedding model normally requires backfilling, and cross-model comparability is a property that has to be trained for.

B1-GEN-01-4.title: Exploiting Similarities among Languages for Machine Translation (Mikolov et al., 2013)
B1-GEN-01-4.supports: Precedent that a linear map can be learned between separately trained embedding spaces (cross-lingual word embeddings); does not establish its adequacy for bridging embedding-model versions.

B1-GEN-01-5.title: When Is Nearest Neighbor Meaningful? (Beyer et al., 1999)
Hubs in Space: Popular Nearest Neighbors in High-Dimensional Data (Radovanovic et al., JMLR 2010)
B1-GEN-01-5.supports: Hubness is reported in high-dimensional data.

B1-GEN-01-6.title: FAISS wiki: Guidelines to choose an index
FAISS wiki: Faiss indexes
B1-GEN-01-6.supports: float16 halves per-vector storage (2*d+8 bytes) and may cause some loss of precision.

B1-GEN-01-6.title: Matryoshka Representation Learning
B1-GEN-01-6.supports: Embeddings explicitly trained for it can be used at lower dimension.

B1-GEN-01-7.title: FAISS wiki: Guidelines to choose an index
B1-GEN-01-7.supports: FAISS gives K=4-16*sqrt(N) as a heuristic for datasets under 1M and recommends a much larger IVF (262144 cells) for 10M-100M, both consistent with raising nlist above 4,096 for 30M vectors.

B1-GEN-03-1.title: Simple Entity-Centric Questions Challenge Dense Retrievers
B1-GEN-03-1.supports: On simple entity-centric questions, dense retrievers drastically underperform sparse methods and generalise mainly to common entities, which is consistent with weakness on rare identifiers (error codes and SKUs were not tested).

B1-GEN-03-1.title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
B1-GEN-03-1.supports: BM25 remains a strong baseline; supports not claiming universal dense superiority.

B1-GEN-03-1.title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion outperforms Condorcet and individual rank learning methods (Cormack et al., SIGIR 2009)

B1-GEN-03-2.title: An Analysis of Fusion Functions for Hybrid Retrieval (Bruch et al.)
B1-GEN-03-2.supports: Convex combination vs RRF and RRF parameter sensitivity.

B1-GEN-03-2.title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion outperforms Condorcet and individual rank learning methods (Cormack et al., SIGIR 2009)

B1-GEN-03-3.title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion outperforms Condorcet and individual rank learning methods (Cormack et al., SIGIR 2009)
B1-GEN-03-3.supports: RRF formula, k=60 origin, and that 60 is a default not a theorem.

B1-GEN-03-3.title: Elasticsearch reference: Reciprocal rank fusion
B1-GEN-03-3.supports: Same formula and default k=60 in a production search engine.

B1-GEN-03-4.title: Lucene BM25Similarity javadoc
B1-GEN-03-4.supports: Defaults, idf formula, and the roles of k1 and b.

B1-GEN-03-4.title: Elastic blog: Practical BM25 part 2 - the algorithm and its variables

B1-GEN-03-5.title: The Use of MMR, Diversity-Based Reranking (Carbonell & Goldstein, 1998)
B1-GEN-03-5.supports: MMR rule and the lambda=1 / lambda=0 limits.

B1-GEN-03-6.title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels (HyDE)
B1-GEN-03-6.supports: HyDE embeds an LLM-written hypothetical document that may contain false details; the paper argues the encoder's dense bottleneck filters most of them out.

B1-GEN-03-6.title: RAG-Fusion: a New Take on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
B1-GEN-03-6.supports: Multi-query generation with reciprocal-rank fusion is a described method (RAG-Fusion) and generated queries that stray from the original can add off-topic results.

B1-GEN-03-6.title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion outperforms Condorcet and individual Rank Learning Methods
B1-GEN-03-6.supports: RRF is a rank-fusion method for combining multiple rankings and generally beats the individual rankers it fuses (about systems, not query variants).

B1-GEN-03-7.title: pgvector README (Filtering section)
B1-GEN-03-7.supports: Post-filtering on an approximate index returns fewer than requested rows for selective filters; exact search suits very selective filters; partitioning/partial indexes and iterative deeper scanning are the documented mitigations.

B1-GEN-03-7.title: Qdrant: Filterable HNSW (article)
B1-GEN-03-7.supports: Applying a restrictive filter during HNSW traversal can break graph connectivity and sharply reduce recall; engines add filter-aware graph construction/search (article describes a 2019 design, not Qdrant's full current behaviour).

B1-GEN-02-2.title: PyMuPDF documentation: Text recipes
B1-GEN-02-2.supports: PDF text extraction follows how content was written to the page, not logical reading order; extractors offer positional sorting or block-level data to rebuild order.

B1-GEN-04-1.title: Sentence-Transformers: Retrieve & Re-Rank
B1-GEN-04-1.supports: A cross-encoder is too slow to score a whole corpus and is used to re-rank a shortlist (e.g. ~100) from a first-stage retriever.

B1-GEN-04-1.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
B1-GEN-04-1.supports: Late-interaction (ColBERT) encodes query and document independently and precomputes document representations offline, so no per-pair transformer pass at query time.

B1-GEN-04-2.title: Sentence-Transformers: Retrieve & Re-Rank
B1-GEN-04-2.supports: A cross-encoder is too slow to score a whole corpus and is used to re-rank a shortlist (e.g. ~100) from a first-stage retriever.

B1-GEN-04-3.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
B1-GEN-04-3.supports: The position-dependent (U-shaped) accuracy effect for long contexts; the abstract gives no mechanism.

B1-GEN-04-4.title: Carbonell & Goldstein 1998, The Use of MMR, Diversity-Based Reranking
B1-GEN-04-4.supports: MMR linearly trades relevance against redundancy via lambda; the paper uses about 0.7 as an illustrative relevance-leaning setting for focusing on reinforcing documents and about 0.3 for broad exploration, and advocates a user-tunable value.

B1-GEN-04-4.title: Broder et al. 1997, On the resemblance and containment of documents
B1-GEN-04-4.supports: Shingle (contiguous token subsequence) overlap, as Jaccard-style resemblance in [0,1], is an established near-duplicate measure; the 0.8 threshold and n=5 are our own choices.

B1-GEN-04-4.title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation (arXiv 2310.04408)
B1-GEN-04-4.supports: Extractive (sentence selection) and abstractive (model-generated summary) compression of retrieved documents are established approaches; the paper does not itself state the risks of dropped qualifiers or altered numbers.

B1-GEN-04-5.title: Evaluating Verifiability in Generative Search Engines (arXiv 2304.09848)
B1-GEN-04-5.supports: Having a citation does not mean the cited source supports the sentence; citation precision and recall are separate properties that must be checked.

B1-GEN-04-5.title: ALCE: Enabling LLMs to Generate Text with Citations (arXiv 2305.14627)
B1-GEN-04-5.supports: Entailment-style (NLI) checking of a statement against its cited passages is an established citation-support evaluation that correlates with human judgement, and a cited passage often does not fully support the statement.

B1-GEN-04-6.title: Claude docs: Context windows
B1-GEN-04-6.supports: System prompt, history and generated output share one window, and on the Claude API an over-long input is rejected with a 400 'prompt is too long' error; silent truncation is not documented there.

B1-GEN-07-1.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts (arXiv 2307.03172)
B1-GEN-07-1.supports: Position of relevant information within the prompt affects answer quality, and extra irrelevant context can hurt.

B1-GEN-07-1.title: Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: Revealing the Behavior of LLMs in Knowledge Conflicts (arXiv 2305.13300)
B1-GEN-07-1.supports: LLMs can be receptive to conflicting external evidence yet show confirmation bias when evidence matches their parametric memory, so parametric override is a plausible cause to test, not a given.

B1-GEN-07-2.title: On Faithfulness and Factuality in Abstractive Summarization (arXiv 2005.00661)
B1-GEN-07-2.supports: Content not supported by the source document (unfaithful) can still be factually true, so faithfulness and correctness are distinct properties.

B1-GEN-07-2.title: Ragas docs: Faithfulness
B1-GEN-07-2.supports: Faithfulness is defined over the response and the retrieved context (not against a reference answer).

B1-GEN-07-3.title: Ragas docs: Faithfulness
B1-GEN-07-3.supports: Faithfulness is defined over the response and the retrieved context (not against a reference answer).

B1-GEN-07-4.title: Sentence Transformers docs: Computing Embeddings (prompts)
B1-GEN-07-4.supports: Some embedding models require specific query/document prompts (e.g. E5 'query: ' / 'passage: ') for best performance, so a model swap may need different prefixes.

B1-GEN-07-4.title: Qdrant docs: Collections (aliases)
B1-GEN-07-4.supports: Qdrant aliases can be repointed atomically at a newly built collection with no impact on concurrent requests (cutover); rollback by repointing is an inference.

B1-GEN-07-4.title: Elasticsearch docs: Aliases
B1-GEN-07-4.supports: Aliases allow reindexing and switching an application between indices without downtime.

B1-GEN-07-5.title: Simple Entity-Centric Questions Challenge Dense Retrievers (arXiv 2109.08535)
B1-GEN-07-5.supports: Dense retrievers underperform sparse (BM25-style) retrieval on rare-entity questions; the paper does not show subword-fragmentation or near-miss ID conflation.

B1-GEN-07-5.title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of IR Models (arXiv 2104.08663)
B1-GEN-07-5.supports: BEIR reports BM25 as a robust zero-shot baseline and that dense/sparse retrievers often underperform other approaches in generalisation; this motivates but does not itself demonstrate benefit from adding lexical retrieval.

B1-GEN-07-5.title: Elasticsearch docs: Reciprocal rank fusion
B1-GEN-07-5.supports: RRF is a standard way to fuse lexical and dense result lists using rank only.

B1-GEN-05-1.title: Koehn 2004, Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
B1-GEN-05-1.supports: Paired bootstrap resampling (resample test items with replacement, score both systems on each resample) is an established method (Koehn 2004); the percentile CI on the mean difference is a standard analogous use.

B1-GEN-05-1.title: Berg-Kirkpatrick et al. 2012, An Empirical Investigation of Statistical Significance in NLP
B1-GEN-05-1.supports: Small test sets need large observed gains to reach significance (shown for MT/parsing F1/BLEU); general principle only, not a threshold for 40 hit@5 queries.

B1-GEN-05-1.title: statsmodels docs: mcnemar
B1-GEN-05-1.supports: McNemar's test on a 2x2 paired table can be computed exactly with the binomial distribution on the discordant cells, matching our sign-test framing (the page does not use the word 'discordant').

B1-GEN-05-2.title: scikit-learn docs: cohen_kappa_score
B1-GEN-05-2.supports: Kappa formula, the marginal-based chance-agreement estimate and the chance-level interpretation of 0 match our calculation. The page says nothing on prevalence effects.

B1-GEN-05-3.title: Ragas docs: Faithfulness
B1-GEN-05-3.supports: Faithfulness is defined over the response and the retrieved context (not against a reference answer).

B1-GEN-05-3.title: Ragas docs: Answer Relevancy
B1-GEN-05-3.supports: Relevance uses question plus answer and does not assess factual accuracy.

B1-GEN-05-3.title: On Faithfulness and Factuality in Abstractive Summarization (arXiv 2005.00661)
B1-GEN-05-3.supports: Content not supported by the source document (unfaithful) can still be factually true, so faithfulness and correctness are distinct properties.

B1-GEN-05-4.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena (arXiv 2306.05685)
B1-GEN-05-4.supports: Position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases exist in LLM judges, vary across judge models, and the both-orders-agree-else-tie rule is a published mitigation. Self-enhancement evidence is explicitly inconclusive.

B1-GEN-05-4.title: Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators (arXiv 2305.17926)
B1-GEN-05-4.supports: Answer order alone can change an LLM evaluator's ranking; aggregating across orders is a mitigation.

B1-GEN-05-4.title: Length-Controlled AlpacaEval (arXiv 2404.04475)
B1-GEN-05-4.supports: Automatic judges can favour longer outputs, and length-controlled comparison is a recognised mitigation.

B1-GEN-05-5.title: BEIR: A Heterogenous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models (Thakur et al., 2021)
B1-GEN-05-5.supports: Annotation pools drawn from lexical systems bias evaluation towards lexical retrievers, and diverse pooling is the remedy.

B1-GEN-05-5.title: Synthetic Test Collections for Retrieval Evaluation (Rahmani et al., 2024)
B1-GEN-05-5.supports: LLM-generated queries differ from real ones: GPT-4-generated queries were longer, had much fewer relevant documents, and synthetic collections tended to be easier; no lexical-leakage or BM25-bias finding.

B1-GEN-05-5.title: How Reliable are the Results of Large-Scale Information Retrieval Experiments? (Zobel, SIGIR 1998)
B1-GEN-05-5.supports: Pooled relevance judgements treat unjudged documents as non-relevant, so systems that did not contribute to the pool may be underestimated; extension to single-gold-chunk sets is by analogy.

B1-GEN-05-6.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts (Liu et al., 2023)
B1-GEN-05-6.supports: Position effect: models use middle-of-context evidence less reliably than evidence at the edges.

B1-GEN-05-7.title: BEIR (Thakur et al., 2021)
B1-GEN-05-7.supports: Unjudged documents count as irrelevant, holes can be annotated, and diverse pooling is the remedy.

B1-GEN-05-7.title: How Reliable are the Results of Large-Scale Information Retrieval Experiments? (Zobel, SIGIR 1998)
B1-GEN-05-7.supports: Pooling bias against systems that did not contribute to the judged pool.

B1-GEN-05-7.title: On the Robustness of Information Retrieval Metrics to Biased Relevance Assessments (Sakai, 2009)
B1-GEN-05-7.supports: Defines condensed lists; shows they are not a guaranteed remedy under biased judgments, so use as a sensitivity check only.

B1-GEN-06-1.title: Weaviate docs: Filtering (concepts)
B1-GEN-06-1.supports: Post-filtering can return nothing for restrictive filters, and engines fall back to flat search of the matching subset.

B1-GEN-06-1.title: Qdrant: Filterable HNSW
B1-GEN-06-1.supports: Applying the filter to graph nodes during search can disconnect the graph and make search fail past a threshold.

B1-GEN-06-1.title: Qdrant docs: Indexing
B1-GEN-06-1.supports: Engines estimate filter cardinality and switch to full scan when a filter is selective.

B1-GEN-06-2.title: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search using Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs (Malkov & Yashunin)
B1-GEN-06-2.supports: Layer-0 degree cap of 2M and the exponentially decaying layer assignment behind the ~1/M node fraction per layer.

B1-GEN-06-2.title: Faiss wiki: Faiss indexes
B1-GEN-06-2.supports: int8 scalar quantisation costs one byte per dimension, PQ code size follows ceil(M*nbits/8), and HNSW adds M*2*4-byte link storage per vector.

B1-GEN-06-3.title: hnswlib README
B1-GEN-06-3.supports: Delete in hnswlib is a mark; the element remains until replaced.

B1-GEN-06-3.title: Weaviate docs: Vector index concepts
B1-GEN-06-3.supports: Deleted vectors stay in the graph until asynchronous cleanup.

B1-GEN-06-3.title: Qdrant docs: Indexing
B1-GEN-06-3.supports: In Qdrant's HNSW, a large number of soft-deleted points can leave the graph with disconnected components and degrade filtered search.

B1-GEN-06-3.title: Lucene TieredMergePolicy javadoc
B1-GEN-06-3.supports: Lucene's TieredMergePolicy tolerates a configurable maximum percentage of deleted documents and favours merges that reclaim deletes (an analogous compaction trigger, not HNSW-specific).

B1-GEN-06-4.title: Elasticsearch guide: Near real-time search
B1-GEN-06-4.supports: Newly written documents become searchable only after a refresh that opens new segments; refresh interval is a freshness knob.

B1-GEN-06-5.title: Qdrant docs: Multitenancy (multiple partitions)
B1-GEN-06-5.supports: Shared partitioned collection for many small tenants, dedicated collections only for a few that need strict isolation, and per-collection overhead.

B1-GEN-06-5.title: Weaviate docs: Data concepts (multi-tenancy)
B1-GEN-06-5.supports: Dedicated per-tenant storage gives isolation and simple tenant erasure.

B1-GEN-06-5.title: Qdrant docs: Indexing
B1-GEN-06-5.supports: Engines fall back to exact scan for very selective filters, as for a small tenant in a shared collection.

B1-GEN-06-6.title: Lucene BM25Similarity javadoc
B1-GEN-06-6.supports: The Lucene idf formula used in the worked example.

B1-GEN-06-6.title: Elastic blog: Practical BM25 Part 1 - How Shards Affect Relevance Scoring in Elasticsearch
B1-GEN-06-6.supports: Shard-local scoring makes scores differ across shards; a global-statistics pre-pass removes the difference at the cost of an extra round trip.

B1-GEN-06-6.title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion outperforms Condorcet and individual Rank Learning Methods (Cormack, Clarke, Buettcher, SIGIR 2009)
B1-GEN-06-6.supports: RRF = sum of 1/(k + rank) with k = 60 as a near-optimal, non-critical default.
